question.problem: Find the maximum value of $Q(\mathbf{x})=2x_1^2 - 5x_2^2 +3x_3^2$ given that $\| \mathbf{x} \| =1.$
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that $x_1^2 \geq 0$ and $x_2^2 \geq 0.$ So, we have that 

$$
2x_1^2 \leq 3x_1^2, \qquad -5x_2^2 \leq 3x_2^2.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =2{x}_{1}^{2}-5{x}_{2}^{2}+3{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & \le 3{x}_{1}^{2}+3{x}_{2}^{2}+3{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =3({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $\| \mathbf{x} \| = 1$ is equivalent to $x_1^2 + x_2^2 + x_3^2 =1.$ So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}3({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2})=3(1)=3,\end{aligned}
$$

and, in turn, $Q(\mathbf{x}) \leq 3.$

So, the value of $Q(\mathbf{x})$ can be no greater than $3.$ But before we conclude that $3$ is the maximum, we need to find a vector such that $Q(\mathbf{x}) = 3.$

Notice that when ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14170041/assets/c4afaf37dc0b68f09e5efac6434f3f22bc8edc107f45ce7f3327c475f4158ea7.svg) we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =2{x}_{1}^{2}-5{x}_{2}^{2}+3{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =2(0)^{2}-5(0)^{2}+3(1)^{2} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, given that $\| \mathbf{x} \| =1,$ the maximum value of $Q(\mathbf{x})$ is equal to $3.$
